evidence: ARITHMETIC (frozen task). task.toml:18 [agent].timeout_sec = 7200.0; :21 build_timeout_sec = 600.0; :27 [verifier].timeout_sec = 13200.0 -- all byte-equal to the template task.toml and staged-task-contract.md lines 53-64. tests/test.sh is byte-identical to the template (diff empty), as are tools/score.py and tests/Dockerfile. Judge timeouts (all batched): gates/render 600 (judge.toml:4), gates/constraints 600, scored/functional 9000, scored/polish 900, scored/visual 900 -- all equal to template values. test.sh:207 runs each suite with `rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1`, so judges in a suite run sequentially and the sum must fit: gates 600+600 = 1200 < 1500 (test.sh:213, margin 300 s); scored 9000+900+900 = 10800 < 11100 (test.sh:224, margin 300 s); every single judge < its suite budget. Suite budgets 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200 verifier (margin 600 s). Liveness: test.sh:116-122 120 x 0.25 s sleep (~30 s nominal; probe urlopen timeout=2 per URL, worst-case hung socket ~510 s, which still nests: 510+12600 = 13110 < 13200, and a non-answering app scores 0 by design). Restart helper waits 30 s (test.sh:171-181) inside restart_mcp.py's 55 s (contract line 163), inside the 9000 s functional judge. Nesting therefore PASSES on every level and matches the reference budgets in staged-task-contract.md:111 (gates 1500, scored 11100, verifier 13200). Agent image (environment/Dockerfile) is small: apt 4 packages + npm express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 (prebuilt binaries for node22) + COPY; 600 s build is plausible though no cold-build timing was supplied. 7200 s agent time is the canonical template value for a hard full-stack build; no measurement contradicts it. SUFFICIENCY ('long enough') IS UNMEASURED. The functional judge (43 criteria, prompt.md 11,180 bytes + judge.toml 15,930 bytes) must execute 13 ordered protocols in one batched session: S creates 2 jobs, 4 refused jobs, 12 candidates and 2 refused adds; M/L/B/R do dozens of individual moves/undos/refusals with multiple independent contexts (Mei Lin, Ingrid, Bill, Aud, Tomas, Noor, anonymous); C/K/R require capture-and-replay of ~10 requests; V and T contain 15 s waits; U, A, D add reading, a restart and a full comparison. Rough estimate: several hundred Playwright MCP tool calls; at roughly 8-15 s per GLM turn+browser action this lands in the ~4,000-9,000 s range, i.e. plausibly near the 9000 s cap. raw-evidence-index.json scope states explicitly: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent' and each entry is 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement.' The scripted golden driver covers 18 groups and is not judge duration (REVIEW_POLICY.md line 25: 'Scripted Playwright duration is not LLM judge duration'). REVIEW_POLICY.md line 31 requires a hash-bound workload record before local clearance; none exists for these bytes. Hence: no demonstrated defect (so not Fail -- the policy forbids inferring workload from a timeout number), budgets correctly unchanged per policy, but the 'long enough' half of the row cannot be cleared and risk stays true. Positive: the task did not touch any template-controlled budget, and nothing was increased automatically.
counterexample: Not a demonstrated defect; the plausible failure mode to measure: a fully conforming golden-quality app whose functional judge needs >9000 s to walk protocols S through D (many UI creates, multi-context sign-ins, replays and 15 s waits) would hit the functional judge timeout or the 11100 s scored budget (test.sh:224 `if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0`), leaving the zero/gate-only record so a correct submission scores 0 -- i.e. the harness, not the submission, would be measured. Conversely a broken app fails early criteria quickly and finishes well within budget, so the timeout would penalise correct apps more than broken ones.
suggested_fix: Run one full configured verifier pass on the golden (and ideally one weak app) on the frozen bytes, record per-suite and per-judge wall time from rewardkit logs in a hash-bound workload record; if functional duration approaches 9000 s, trim redundant protocol steps (e.g. duplicate refused-job variants, repeated replays) together with matching public scope, or obtain explicit authorization for a justified sub-5-hour budget change with the checker adapted narrowly.
